description: Shokupan is a beloved Japanese milk bread, renowned for its incredibly soft, fluffy texture and delicate sweetness. Achieved through the tangzhong method, this loaf boasts a fine crumb and a satisfying chewiness that makes it perfect for sandwiches, toast, or simply enjoyed on its own. Its golden crust and cloud-like interior are a testament to the meticulous art of Japanese baking.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tangzhong (Water Roux)
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, whisk together 25g water, 25g milk, and 10g bread flour until smooth. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens to a paste-like consistency, about 2-3 minutes. It should reach 65C (149F). Remove from heat, transfer to a small bowl, cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface to prevent a skin from forming, and let cool completely to room temperature. This can be done in advance and refrigerated.

instructions.title: Combine Dry Ingredients
instructions.text: In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine 250g bread flour, granulated sugar, salt, and instant dry yeast. Whisk briefly to combine these dry ingredients evenly.

instructions.title: Add Wet Ingredients and Initial Mix
instructions.text: Add the cooled tangzhong, 80g lukewarm milk, and 25g beaten egg to the dry ingredients. Attach the dough hook to your stand mixer and mix on low speed for about 2-3 minutes, or until a shaggy, cohesive dough forms.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Increase the mixer speed to medium-low and knead for about 10-12 minutes, or until the dough starts to come together and is somewhat smooth. Add the 25g softened unsalted butter and continue kneading for another 8-10 minutes, until the dough is smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test (a small piece can be stretched thinly without tearing).

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Form the dough into a ball and place it in a lightly oiled bowl. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until the dough has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape the Loaf
instructions.text: Gently punch down the dough to release air. Transfer it to a lightly floured surface and divide the dough into three equal pieces. Roll each piece into an oval, then fold the top third down and the bottom third up, pressing to seal. Turn the dough 90 degrees and roll it into a long cylinder. Place the three cylinders seam-side down into a greased 9x4x4 inch loaf pan.

instructions.title: Second Proofing and Preheat Oven
instructions.text: Cover the loaf pan with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for another 45-60 minutes, or until the dough reaches about 1 inch below the rim of the pan. During the last 15 minutes of this proofing stage, preheat your oven to 190C (375F).

instructions.title: Bake the Shokupan
instructions.text: Lightly brush the top of the risen dough with a bit of milk or an egg wash for a beautiful golden crust. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped. If the top browns too quickly, loosely tent the loaf with aluminum foil to prevent over-browning.

instructions.title: Cooling
instructions.text: Remove the loaf from the oven and immediately turn it out onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing. This crucial step prevents the bottom from becoming soggy and ensures the bread maintains its signature soft texture throughout.

tips: The tangzhong (water roux) is crucial for the signature softness and extended freshness of Shokupan. Ensure it cools completely before adding to the main dough.
Achieving a good windowpane test during kneading is key. Don't rush this process, as proper gluten development ensures a fluffy, elastic texture.

For the best texture and to prevent a soggy bottom, allow the Shokupan to cool completely on a wire rack for at least 1 hour before slicing. Store in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 3 days.
